notes:
Rust workspace, crates/blind is the TUI binary. Rules: no comments, small functions, one component per file, clippy -D warnings (workspace lints: unsafe_code forbid, clippy::all deny, wildcard_enum_match_arm deny, so every `match` on Action/Speaker/Status must list variants). Tests live next to code in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. Fixtures are `pub(crate) mod test_support` (e.g. backend::test_support::offline, chain_backend::test_support::unable_to_run).

Conversation (conversation.rs): `entries: Vec<Entry{speaker: Speaker(Human|Root|Chain), text}>`, `status: Status(Idle|Waiting|Answering|Failed(String))`. `say` pushes Human and sets Waiting. `delegate` pushes Human with no Waiting. `report` pushes Chain. `receive(ReplyEvent::Text)` appends to the last Root entry while Answering, otherwise pushes a new Root entry, and sets Answering. `Done` and `Failed` set Idle or Failed. The raw model text is in `Entry.text`, so wrapping and labels are added only in chat_view. last_answer and last_exchange must be added here. A reply is finished only if the last Root entry is not currently streaming (status Answering means the last Root entry is unfinished). A Failed status leaves a partial Root entry. A Chain entry or a delegated Human task can sit between a prompt and its answer, because Human entries come from both `say` and `delegate`. The planner must decide how to pair prompt and answer. The existing tests use helpers asked/text/texts. The architecture test forbids std::fs and std::process in conversation.rs and backend.rs.

Keys: tui/keys.rs maps KeyEvent to `Action` (Insert(char) carries 'y' and 'Y'; shift-Y arrives as Char('Y')). Ctrl-X gives Action::Leader. In tui/app.rs `App::handle` sets `awaiting_command`, and then `run_command(action)` handles the next key with consts SIDEBAR_KEY 's', CHAIN_KEY 'c', digits via Tab::numbered. New copy keys go there. `App` has the `notice: Option<String>` field, but it is shown only by settings_view. Nothing clears it on a keypress. A status message must show in the status line and clear on the next key, so `handle` needs to reset it at the start. App tests: `app(&dir)`/`app_with`, press keys via `app.handle(ctrl('x'))`, `letter('y')`.

Status line: tui/status_line.rs `StatusLine::new(model, usage, hint, theme)` renders text from fixed fallbacks by width. tui.rs `draw` builds it with `hint(app)`. Hints are consts there: KEYS_HINT, READING_HINT, COMMAND_HINT = "1 root · 2 settings · 3 chain · c build chain · s sidebar" (the hint shown after Ctrl-X, where y and Y must be added), BUILDER_HINT, SIDEBAR_HINT. Tests use `screen(app)` and `assert_shows`. tui.rs tests reference the hint consts.

Clipboard: needs a new module, outside tui/. tests/architecture.rs `screen_cannot_reach_the_network_the_filesystem_or_the_worker_loop` scans tui/*.rs and tui.rs production code and forbids `std::process`, `std::fs`, `std::net`, `tokio`, `reqwest` and `crate::providers/step/chain_run/agents`. So a pbcopy/OSC52 implementation (std::process or writing to the terminal) must live in a new top-level module such as crates/blind/src/clipboard.rs (register `mod clipboard;` in main.rs, alphabetical list). It needs a trait or struct plus a test fake, injected into the tui via the `Services` struct (tui/app.rs, fields backend, chain_backend, crew) and constructed in session.rs `run()`. Services is also built in tui.rs tests and app.rs tests, so both need updating. A fake lives in `clipboard::test_support` following the existing pattern. Choice of mechanism is open: pbcopy via std::process works inside zellij on macOS. OSC 52 depends on zellij passthrough. Dependencies are in crates/blind/Cargo.toml: no clipboard crate present (ratatui 0.30, crossterm via ratatui, textwrap, tokio, anyhow, thiserror). unsafe is forbidden. Also keep CI on ubuntu-latest in mind (.github/workflows/ci.yml runs fmt, clippy -D warnings, test on ubuntu and macos).

README.md line ~49 has the 'Keys in the TUI' paragraph, where Ctrl-X y and Ctrl-X Y must be added. evals/copy-blocks/README.md and task.md describe the eval only (acceptance tests will be added later in the copy and call Conversation::last_answer(&self) -> Option<&str> and last_exchange(&self) -> Option<String>). chat_view.rs renders labels `you`/`root` and wraps via textwrap, which is why the copy must read entries, not the screen.
